Research article 
Evaluating the impact of technological development policy on the 
high-quality development of the manufacturing industry: 
Mechanisms and threshold effects 
Borui Yan a,*, Yamin Wang b 
a School of Economics and Management, Xianyang Normal University, Xianyang, China b School of Primary Education, Changsha Normal University, Changsha, 410100, Hunan, China 
ARTICLE INFO 
JEL classification: 
E620 
Keywords: 
Technological development policy 
High-quality development of the 
manufacturing industry 
High-tech industry 
Industrial structure 
ABSTRACT 
As the world’s largest manufacturing country, the rapid growth of China’s manufacturing industry has historically relied on factor input. To achieve high-quality development of the 
manufacturing industry, China must accelerate the transformation from extensive factor input to 
innovation. The purpose of this study is to further explore the impact mechanisms of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry. It 
selected data from 30 provinces and cities in China spanning from 2011 to 2021 for the study. 
Initially, it established a benchmark regression model to verify the positive impact of technological development policies on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry. 
Subsequently, a mediation effect model was used to analyze the role of high-tech industry 
development in mediating this impact, and a moderation effect model was applied to study the 
moderating effect of the level of infrastructure informatization. Additionally, taking the industrial 
structure as a threshold variable, a panel threshold effect model was employed to explore the 
impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the 
manufacturing industry. It was found that enhancing the level of high-tech industries further 
facilitates the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry through technological 
development policy. The level of infrastructure informatization positively moderates the impact

of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry. Moreover, the industrial structure exhibits a threshold effect in this impact. 
1. Introduction 
As the world’s largest manufacturing country, China has experienced rapid development in its manufacturing industry since the 
commencement of economic reforms in 1978. However, this growth has largely depended on factor inputs. To achieve high-quality 
development in manufacturing, China must accelerate its transition from a mode driven by extensive factor inputs to one driven by 
innovation [1,2]. Investment in technological innovation promotes technical advancement and is widely regarded as a key factor for 
manufacturing enterprises to gain competitive advantages [3]. In practice, governments around the world are formulating and 
implementing a series of technological development policies to foster high-quality development in manufacturing. For example, the

Chinese government’s “Made in China 2025″ strategic plan aims to promote the high-end, intelligent, and green development of the 
manufacturing industry through technological upgrading and industrial transformation. Similarly, the German government’s “Industry 4.0″ strategic plan aims to enhance the digitalization and intelligence of the manufacturing industry [4]. The implementation of 
these policy measures has yielded significant results, effectively driving the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry in 
their respective countries. Moreover, higher government quality stimulates innovation activities in enterprises [5]. 
As an important national strategic initiative, technological development policy aims to promote high-quality, efficient, and highvalue-added development of the manufacturing industry by guiding technological innovation and optimizing resource allocation 
[6–9]. On one hand, policies can direct the flow of funds by providing essential research and development funding to manufacturing 
enterprises. On the other hand, policies can stimulate market demand by promoting new products and applications, thereby expanding

the scale of market demand and driving the development of manufacturing enterprises. Additionally, policies can incentivize enterprises to increase investment in technological innovation and enhance their core competitiveness through tax incentives, reward 
measures, and other mechanisms [10]. 
However, the impact of technological development policy is not static; it varies with the different stages of manufacturing 
development and diverse industrial structures [11]. In the early stages of manufacturing development, technology policies may focus 
more on basic research and infrastructure construction. As manufacturing progresses, these policies may shift towards 
innovation-driven approaches and industrial collaboration, encouraging deep integration of manufacturing with other industries to 
enhance and upgrade the industrial chain [12]. Especially for high-tech industries, the impact of technology policies is more significant 
[13]. High-tech industries typically represent the core competitiveness and future development direction of a country’s manufacturing 
industry. By implementing targeted technology policies, such as specialized funding support, tax incentives, and support for research 
and development, governments can significantly promote the growth of high-tech industries, thereby driving the high-quality 
development of the manufacturing industry [14]. At the same time, the impact of technological development policy is not always 
positive. Inappropriate technology policies can distort market mechanisms and lead to the irrational allocation of resources [11]. 
Additionally, excessive government intervention may suppress the innovation vitality of enterprises and negatively affect the 
development of the manufacturing industry [15]. Therefore, when formulating technology policies, governments need to scientifically 
evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of these policies to ensure they genuinely promote the high-quality development of the 
manufacturing industry [16–18]. 
The mechanism and pathways through which technological development policy affects the high-quality development of the 
manufacturing industry still require further exploration. In light of this, this paper conducts an in-depth analysis of how technological 
development policy impacts the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry. 
It first established a benchmark regression model to verify the positive impact of technological development policy on the highquality development of the manufacturing industry. Subsequently, it established a model to validate the mediating effect of hightech industry development on this relationship, as well as the moderating effect of infrastructure informatization in the process. 
Additionally, it analyzed the impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry at different industry structure thresholds.

The subsequent sections are organized as follows: the second section covers related literature and hypotheses, the third section 
introduces the research methodology, the fourth section discusses the research results, and the fifth section presents conclusions and 
discussion. 
2. Literature review and hypotheses 
The high-quality development of the manufacturing industry is a crucial component of China’s high-quality economic development. It is guided by the new development concept, driven by innovation, and characterized by efficiency and benefits. Achieving 
high-quality development in manufacturing entails low production factor input, efficient resource allocation, strong product quality 
improvement capabilities, excellent ecological environment quality, and favorable economic and social benefits, thus ensuring sustainable development at a high level [19]. It focuses on enhancing the vitality, driving force, innovation, and competitiveness of the 
economy, continuously improving input-output efficiency and economic benefits. Its goal and mission are to shift from “scale 
expansion” to “quality and efficiency improvement,” transitioning from traditional manufacturing models to new models such as 
intelligent manufacturing, green manufacturing, and service-oriented manufacturing, and upgrading from a traditional industrial 
system to a modern industrial system. Technological progress and innovation are crucial forces driving the high-quality development 
of manufacturing [20]. 
Manufacturing enterprises are considered the primary drivers of economic growth, and the efficient design of institutional environments and their evolution over time are crucial for explaining national development stages and economic performance [21,22], 
indirectly confirming the significance of government policy orientation for manufacturing development. As the prominence of the 
manufacturing industry in the global economy continues to grow, the driving force of technological progress on industrial development is increasingly emphasized. This has made the relationship between technological development policy and high-quality 
development in manufacturing a hot topic in academic research. When formulating industrial policies, governments need to meet 
two basic conditions: ensuring adequate competitiveness of target industries and benefiting a sufficiently broad range of enterprises. 
This implies that policies should not only foster the growth of specific industries but also ensure their competitiveness and sustainability [23]. Government intervention plays a crucial role in promoting the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry. It 
guides the reconfiguration and allocation of industrial resources through industrial transformation policies, enhances market supervision, establishes platforms for industrial transformation service, and creates a conducive environment for high-quality development

[24]. Therefore, the government assumes roles as a “designer”, “referee”, and “service provider”. Empirical research on government 
behavior in industrial transformation and upgrading confirms that government functions, industrial policies, and government investments can effectively promote these processes [25]. 
For the direct impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry, scholars 
generally assert that technology policies, including provisions such as research and development funding support, tax incentives, and 
market promotion, effectively stimulate technological innovation and industrial upgrading within manufacturing enterprises. These 
innovations and technological advancements can elevate the production technology and process standards of the manufacturing industry, thereby enhancing product quality. This approach of driving industry high-quality development through innovation has been 
widely recognized [26]. The government’s technological development policy measures not only reduce enterprises’ research and 
development costs and market risks but also stimulate their innovation vitality and competitiveness, thereby driving the high-quality 
development of the manufacturing industry. From the perspective of fiscal technology investment, Cen et al. [27] theoretically 
demonstrated that the policy effect of China’s implementation of an innovation-driven development strategy is significant, and will 
become increasingly evident in the context of high-quality development. Chen et al. indicated that the government’s increased fiscal 
investment in technology significantly promotes enterprise innovation output [28]. Jain et al. pointed out that the government’s 
provision of discounted internet facilities, fiscal support, and continuous professional skill training are the primary driving factors for 
the application of Industry 4.0 in the manufacturing industry in India, as they possess strong driving forces [29]. Ullah et al. indicated 
that “cost reduction” and “government support” are the most significant driving forces behind the implementation of green innovation 
in Pakistan’s manufacturing industry [30]. In the absence of financing constraints, technological innovation can significantly advance 
the high-level development of China’s manufacturing industry [31]. Government actions are widely recognized as crucial factors 
influencing the transformation and upgrading of the manufacturing industry [32]. Moreover, technological development policies 
typically drive the digitalization and intelligent transformation of the manufacturing industry, promoting automation and intelligence 
in production process, enhancing production efficiency and product quality, and thereby achieving high-quality development in

manufacturing [33,34].Based on these points, we propose Hypothesis 1. 
Hypothesis 1. Technological development policy positively impacts the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry. 
When studying the impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry, 
many scholars have also explored how specific innovation policies, such as financial subsidies and tax incentives, influence enterprise 
innovation [35]. Some studies suggest that government subsidies [36] and tax incentives [37] significantly enhance both enterprise 
innovation and the steady growth of productivity [38] as well as improve total factor productivity [39]. Desai and Hines, as well as 
Girma et al., have confirmed that subsidies can also enhance enterprise profitability [10,40]. 
However, some studies have indicated that the effectiveness of technology policies is influenced by various factors, such as policy 
design, implementation intensity, and market environment, etc. Therefore, it is necessary to comprehensively consider these factors in 
practical operations to ensure the effectiveness and sustainability of policies [41]. Yang et al. argued that overall, financial subsidies 
and tax incentives have significantly promoted innovation activities among manufacturing enterprises in China. However, there are 
differences in the effectiveness of these two policies, with financial subsidies showing a notably superior incentive effect compared of 
tax incentives [42]. Factors such as enterprise type, industry, region, financing constraints, and the lifecycle of the enterprise also 
moderate the impact of government subsidies [43,44]. Additionally, the incentive effect of fiscal policies positively impact the increase 
in value-added rates and the optimization of internal structures in high-tech industries [36]. The study by Ye and Liu indicated that the 
technological advancement in mid-to-low-end manufacturing industries primarily depends on the continuous improvement of marketization levels, whereas government support effectively promotes technological advancement in high-end manufacturing industries 
[45]. It is evident that technological development policy contributes to the advancement of high-tech industries. The development of 
high-tech industries may lead to effects such as technological innovation, improvements in production processes, and enhancements in 
product quality. These effects translate into technological upgrading, improved product quality, and industrial transformation within 
the manufacturing industry, thereby promoting its high-quality development [46]. Based on these, hypothesis 2 is proposed.

Hypothesis 2. Technological development policy promotes the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry through its 
impact on the development of high-tech industries, specifically through the mediating effect of high-tech industry development in the 
relationship between technological development policy and high-quality development of the manufacturing industry. 
The level of infrastructure informatization typically denotes the extent of digitalization and information technology integration 
within the infrastructure industry of a country or region, encompassing digital infrastructure and information technology applications. 
Xu and Fan suggested that the pathway of indigenous innovation based on internet technology introduction has the most significant 
impact on optimizing and upgrading the structure of the manufacturing industry. This pathway represents the optimal approach for 
driving structural adjustments in China’s manufacturing industry [47]. Hu et al. further emphasized that the internet has a significant 
positive impact on transforming technological pathways in the manufacturing industry. With the deepening development and 
application of the internet, the technological pathway shifts from mere introduction and imitation to independent research and 
development. This transformation enhances its positive effects on improving production efficiency and becomes a suitable technological pathway for achieving high-quality development of the manufacturing industry [48]. In addition, the study by Song and Liu 
indicated that technological progress, optimization of energy structure, and adjustment of industrial structure constitute the mechanisms through which the innovation level in infrastructure construction affects the carbon emission intensity of the manufacturing 
industry. The innovation level in infrastructure construction exhibits a spatial effect on the carbon emission intensity of the 
manufacturing industry, characterized by spatial spillover effects and spatial siphon effects, with distinct regional boundaries for these

spatial effects [49]. In the development of the manufacturing industry, digital infrastructure (such as networks, cloud computing, and 
the Internet of Things) forms the foundation for digitizing and smartening production processes [50] Regions with higher levels of 
informatization typically possess stronger capabilities in information technology application, enabling them to optimize production 
processes and improve product quality more effectively [1]. The improvement of digital infrastructure can enhance support for policy 
implementation, such as digital supervision and data sharing, thereby effectively promoting the high-quality development of the

manufacturing industry [51] The investment and transformation capabilities of the manufacturing industry in digitization and intelligence directly influence the speed and effectiveness of its high-quality development. Manufacturing industries in regions with high 
levels of informatization may demonstrate greater capacity to adapt digital and intelligent production methods, enabling them to 
respond more promptly to policy directives [52]. Based on these, we propose Hypothesis 3. 
Hypothesis 3. The level of infrastructure informatization moderates the impact of technological development policy on the highquality development of the manufacturing industry. 
While many studies suggested that policies such as government subsidies and tax incentives have a positive impact on enterprise 
innovation and technological progress, there are also scholars who hold different views. They argued that government subsidies may 
not effectively enhance the innovation capability of enterprises and may instead foster an overreliance on policies, potentially 
diverting attention away from market competition [53]. Government subsidies do not always have a positive impact on industry target 
parameters and may even distort market mechanisms (Korovin, 2021). In the emerging field of Industry 4.0, which holds significant 
importance for China’s industrial upgrading and improving the quality of manufacturing development, research by Lin et al. found that 
government subsidies do not significantly influence enterprises’ decisions regarding Industry 4.0 adoption [54]. From an overall 
perspective, government subsidies have a certain inhibitory effect on the improvement of enterprise development quality. However, 
government subsidies can also incentivize enterprises to innovate, thereby exerting a positive impact on the quality of enterprise 
development. This effect manifests as a masking effect, where the positive indirect effects of enterprise innovation somewhat mitigate 
the negative impact of government subsidies’ direct effects [55]. Additionally, some studies have indicated that although government 
subsidies can significantly accelerate industrial structural changes, the effects of these changes are short-term. This may be due to 
government subsidy policies not effectively adapting to market dynamics, thus failing to realize long-term effects [56]. The study by Fu 
et al. also pointed out that while independent innovation can rationalize the structure of the manufacturing industry, it may not 
necessarily promote its upgrading [57]. 
Taking into account the diverse development needs and bottlenecks of the manufacturing industry at different stages of industrial

structure development, the focus and effectiveness of technology policies will also vary [58]. In the early stage of rationalizing industrial structure, the manufacturing industry is primarily composed of traditional manufacturing. During this phase, technology 
policies mainly focus on improving the technological level and production efficiency of traditional manufacturing, encouraging enterprises to undertake technological transformations and upgrades. Policies such as technology transfer, fiscal subsidies, and tax incentives can be adopted. As the rationalization of industrial structure progresses, the manufacturing industry begins to transition to 
high-end manufacturing, with increasing demands on technological levels. It needs to pay more attention to the combination of 
basic research and applied research, strengthen the research and promotion of key core technologies, and promote the development of 
the manufacturing industry towards high technology and high value-added directions. It also needs to focus on talent cultivation and 
recruitment to provide sufficient support of high-tech talents for the manufacturing industry. In the stage of a highly rationalized 
industrial structure, the manufacturing industry is mainly composed of emerging industries such as smart manufacturing and green

manufacturing, which have higher requirements for technological innovation. At this stage, it needs to pay more attention to 
cross-disciplinary integration and collaborative innovation, promoting the deep integration of the manufacturing industry with fields 
such as the internet, big data, and artificial intelligence, thereby enhancing the levels of intelligence and greenness in manufacturing 
[59]. Additionally, it needs to focus on nurturing and developing emerging industries to provide a continuous source of momentum for

Hypothesis 4. The impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry 
varies across different stages of industrial structural development. 
These hypotheses (Fig. 1) provide a theoretical foundation for further empirical research, contributing to a deeper understanding of 
the mechanisms and influencing factors of how technological development policy affects the high-quality development of the 
manufacturing industry. 
3. Research design 
3.1. Model construction 
3.1.1. Benchmark regression and mediation model 
To thoroughly analyze the direct impact mechanism of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the

manufacturing industry, as well as the mediating effect of high-tech industries in this process, the following recursive mediation model 
is constructed: 
hqmi，t = α0 + α1tii,t + α2Xi,t + μi + γt + εi,t (1) 
hri，t = β0 + β1tii,t + β2Xi,t + μi + γt + εi,t (2) 
hqmi，t = δ0 + δ1tii,t + δ2hii,t + δ3Xi,t + μi + γt + εi,t (3) 
Where the dependent variable hqm represents the level of high-quality development of the manufacturing industry, the core 
explanatory variable ti represents the level of technological development policy, hr is the mediating variable, and X represents the 
control variables. The subscripts i and t respectively represent the region and the year, μi indicates individual fixed effects, γt indicates 
time fixed effects, εi,t represents the random disturbance term. The term α0 represents the constant term, α1 represents the regression 
coefficient of the core explanatory variable, reflecting the impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry, and α2 represents the regression coefficient of the control variable. Model (1) examines the direct 
impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry, while models (2) and (3) 
examine the mediating effects of high-tech industry development. 
3.1.2. Moderation effect model 
This paper constructs the following models to examine whether the level of infrastructure informatization acts as a moderator in the 
process of how technological development policy influences the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry: 
hqmi，t = θ0 + θ1tii,t + θ2besi,t + θ3Xi,t + μi + γt + εi,t (4) 
where, besi,t is the moderating variable, representing the level of infrastructure informatization, and the remaining variables are as 
before. 
3.1.3. Panel threshold effect model 
Taking into account the varying degree of industrial structure rationalization, the impact of technological development policy on

the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry also varies. To verify this mechanism, this paper adopts Hansen’s proposed threshold regression model for analysis. If only one threshold exists, a single-threshold model is used.

3.2. Variable description and data sources 
3.2.1. Dependent and core explanatory variables 
The dependent variable in this study is the level of high-quality development of the manufacturing industry (hqm), assessed using 
the entropy method derived from the indicator system in Table 1. The core explanatory variable is the level of technological development policy (ti), defined as the ratio of financial expenditure allocated to scientific and technological initiatives relative to overall 
financial expenditure [60].

3.2.2. Mediating, moderating, and threshold variables 
The mediating variable is the development of high-tech industries (hr), indicated by the ratio of main business income of high-tech 
industries to main business income of industrial enterprises above designated size. The moderating variable is the level of infrastructure informatization, represented by the number of websites per hundred enterprises (bes). The threshold variable is the level of 
industrial structure rationalization (isr), calculated using the Theil index, where a higher value indicates a higher degree of industrial 
structure irrationality [61]. 
3.2.3. Control variables 
Infrastructure level (pcrm) is represented by per capita road mileage; Manufacturing scale (gg) is represented by the ratio of industrial value added to GDP; Government intervention level (lfeg) is represented by the ratio of local fiscal general budget expenditure 
to GDP; Human capital level (ae) is represented by the average number of employees in high-tech industries [62,63]. 
3.2.4. Data sources and descriptive statistics 
Due to incomplete data in Tibet, Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan, this study selected data from 30 provinces and cities in China 
from 2011 to 2021 for analysis. The data primarily sourced from publications such as the “China Statistical Yearbook,” “China Energy 
Statistical Yearbook,” and “China Environmental Statistical Yearbook.” Interpolation was employed to fill in missing original data. The 
descriptive statistical results of the primary variables are detailed in Table 2. 
4. Empirical results and analysis 
4.1. Benchmark regression 
Using STATA 17.0 software, it conducted F-tests and Hausman tests on the baseline model to select a two-way fixed effects model 
for examining the mechanism of the technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry. 
Table 3 reports the results of the benchmark regression. In column (1), without considering control variables, technological development policy significantly impacts the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry at the 1 % significance level. Column 
(2), after including control variables such as infrastructure construction level, manufacturing scale, government intervention level, and

human capital level, continues to show a significant positive impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry, thus confirming hypothesis 1. Government influences the manufacturing industry’s development through various technological development policies, including financial support, market demand creation, and incentivizing 
enterprise innovation, which enhance the technological levels, product quality, and market competitiveness of the manufacturing 
industry, thereby promoting high-quality development in the manufacturing industry.

4.2. Mediating effect test 
The columns (3) and (4) in Table 4 present the regression results with high-tech industry development as the mediator. In column 
(3), high-tech industry development shows a significantly positive impact at the 1 % significance level, indicating that technological 
development policy has a significant positive impact on the development of high-tech industries. This fosters innovation activities and 
technological progress in high-tech industries, thereby supporting their rapid development. Column (4), even after including the

mediating variable, high-tech industry development remains significantly positive. Additionally, the coefficient of technological 
development policy decreases compared to the benchmark regression. This suggests that high-tech industry development acts as a 
mediator in the relationship between technological development policy and the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry. In other words, technological development policy promotes the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry by 
enhancing the level of high-tech industry development, thus confirming hypothesis 2. 
4.3. Moderating effect test 
The theoretical analysis in previous sections suggests that the level of infrastructure informatization may play a significant role as a 
moderating variable in the relationship between technological development policy and the high-quality development of the 
manufacturing industry. To explore this, we introduced it into the baseline model and exmined the impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry by including an interaction term between technological 
development policy and the level of infrastructure informatization. To mitigate multicollinearity, the interaction term was centered. 
The results of the moderating effect are reported in Table 5. The column (3) represents the moderating effect of the level of infrastructure informatization. The results indicate that the interaction term between technological development policy and the level of 
infrastructure informatization is significant at the 5 % significance level. Moreover, the coefficient sign of the core explanatory variable 
aligns with that of the interaction term. This indicates that the level of infrastructure informatization strengthens the promotional

4.4. Threshold effect test 
In this study, the bootstrap method was used to sample 300 times to test the case where industrial structure rationalization acts as 
the threshold variable. The results are shown in Table 6. Among them, the P-values for the single threshold, double threshold, and 
triple threshold models are 0.0033, 0.0467, and 0.2600, respectively. This indicates that the double threshold for industrial structure 
rationalization is significant at the 5 % significance level, while the triple threshold is not. The P-value for the single threshold is 
0.0697, and for the double threshold, it is 0.9575. 
The estimation results of the double-panel threshold are shown in Table 7. The regression results indicate that when the Theil index

is relatively small (isr ≤0.0697), indicating a higher level of industrial structure rationalization, the effect of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry is not significant. When the Theil index value is 0.0697 <
isr ≤0.99319, the coefficient is 0.0181. When the Theil index is relatively large (0.99319 < isr), indicating a lower level of industrial 
structure rationalization, the coefficient is 0.0265. These results demonstrate that when the industrial structure is more irrational, the 
impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry is more significant. 
Conversely, when the industrial structure is more rational, the impact is insignificant. In other words, the industrial structure exhibits a 
threshold effect in the impact of technological development policy on the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry, 
validating Hypothesis 4. 
4.5. Robustness test 
Although the two-way fixed effects model used in the benchmark regression partially addresses endogeneity, it still inevitably 
suffers from endogeneity issues due to omitted variables or reverse causality. Therefore, this study substitutes the full-time equivalent 
of R&D personnel in industrial enterprises above a designated size for technological development policy as the core explanatory 
variable. It substitutes the number of patent applications by industrial enterprises above a designated size for the level of development 
of high-tech industry development as the mediating variable. Furthermore, the number of domain names is used as the moderating 
variable instead of the number of websites per hundred enterprises for empirical testing. The results show that the robustness check 
results are generally consistent with the empirical conclusions in the previous sections, confirming the reliability of the empirical tests 
conducted in this study. 
5. Discussion 
The findings of this study provide significant insights into the relationship between technological development policy and the highquality development of the manufacturing industry. 
(1) Promoting role of technological development policy: The benchmark regression results underscore the pivotal role of technological development policy in fostering the high-quality development of the manufacturing sector. This aligns with prior 
studies that have highlighted the importance of policy frameworks in driving industrial advancement and innovation. For 
instance, Bekhet et al. emphasized that transitioning from extensive factor inputs to innovation-driven growth is crucial for

sustainable development in manufacturing [26]. Our findings reinforce the notion that well-crafted technology policies can 
significantly enhance industrial performance.

(2) Mechanism through high-tech industry development: The mechanism analysis results suggest that the enhancement of hightech industries is a key pathway through which technology development policies exert their positive influence. This finding 
is consistent with literature indicating that investment in high-tech industries catalyzes broader industrial growth and 
competitiveness [61]. It highlights the necessity for policymakers to focus on nurturing high-tech industries as a strategic 
approach to elevate overall industrial quality. 
(3) Moderating effect of infrastructure informatization: The moderation effect analysis reveals that the level of infrastructure 
informatization amplifies the positive impact of technological development policies. This finding is particularly relevant in the 
context of the digital economy, where digital infrastructure serves as a backbone for industrial innovation and efficiency. The 
results suggest that investments in digital infrastructure are critical to maximizing the benefits of technology policies, supporting the conclusions drawn by Yin et al. [16]. 
(4) Threshold effect of industrial structure: The threshold effect results provide a nuanced understanding of how industrial 
structure mediates the impact of technological development policies. When the industrial structure is more irrational, the

policies have a more pronounced effect on high-quality development. Conversely, in a more rational industrial structure, the 
impact diminishes. This finding offers a fresh perspective on the dynamic interplay between policy interventions and structural 
conditions within the industry. It suggests that policy effectiveness may vary depending on the maturity and rationality of the 
industrial structure, a notion supported by studies on industrial policy and structural transformation [63]. 
6. Conclusions and implications 
In summary, through a comprehensive analysis of the relationship between technological development policies and the highquality development of the manufacturing industry, it has drawn the following conclusions. 
(1) Technological development policies play a crucial role in promoting the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry, providing strong guidance and support for its innovation and upgrading. 
(2) The development of high-tech industries serves as a significant driving force for promoting the high-quality development of the 
manufacturing industry. Policy makers should increase their support for high-tech industries to enhance their leading role in the 
manufacturing sector. 
(3) The enhancement of the level of infrastructure informatization has a significant role in promoting the high-quality development 
of the manufacturing industry. Governments should continue to increase investment in digital infrastructure construction and 
promote its deep integration with the manufacturing industry. 
(4) The threshold effect of industrial structure indicates that in formulating technology development policies, it is necessary to 
consider the characteristics and needs of different industrial structures. Policy makers should flexibly adjust policy directions 
and intensities based on the changing trends of specific industrial structures. 
Based on the above research conclusions, it proposes the following policy recommendations. 
(1) Strengthen the orientation of technological development policies. The government should continue formulating and implementing policies that support technological development, such as providing research funds, tax incentives, innovation rewards, 
etc. For regions with irrational industrial structures, intensify the implementation of technological development policies. For 
regions with rational industrial structures, adjust policy directions appropriately to avoid over-reliance on technological 
development policies. 
(2) Improve local government policies on investment in high-tech industries. Expand financing channels for technology companies

and encourage various financial institutions to increase their investment in technology companies through loans, equity investments, etc. Increase loan sizes for technology companies to alleviate the financing difficulties faced by small and mediumsized enterprises. Increase financial support and raise the proportion of investment in technology funds, especially for research 
and development projects in key areas and important industries. Provide necessary assistance and support for important industries undergoing upgrades and breakthroughs. 
(3) Strengthen infrastructure informatization construction. Increase investment in infrastructure, especially in infrastructure 
informatization, to enhance the quality and coverage. Optimize the investment structure to improve investment efficiency and 
avoid redundant construction and resource wastage. 
(4) Optimize industrial policies. Guide industrial structure adjustment by providing tax incentives, subsidies, etc., to encourage the 
development of high-tech industry, while limiting or eliminating outdated production capacities. Promote the development of 
industrial clusters to leverage economies of scale and enhance the overall competitiveness of the industrial chain. 
(5) Strengthen intellectual property protection. Improve intellectual property laws and regulations, enact stricter laws to enhance 
enforcement and ensure the effective protection of innovative achievements. Establish an intellectual property trading platform 
to encourage the public opening of technical assets, facilitating technology transfer and commercialization through intellectual 
property transactions. 
(6) Enhance policy coordination and cooperation. Strengthen coordination and cooperation with other relevant policies such as 
fiscal policy, industrial policy, environmental protection policy, etc., to create synergize efforts and collectively promote the 
high-quality development of the manufacturing industry.

(7) Improve the science and technology innovation service system. Establish a science and technology innovation service platform 
to provide services such as technology transfer, intellectual property protection, and financing support to help companies 
address practical issues in the process of technological innovation. Promote industry-university-research cooperation by 
encouraging collaboration between universities, research institutions, and enterprises to jointly undertake research and 
development projects, facilitating the transformation and application of scientific and technological innovations. 
(8) Establish a comprehensive policy evaluation and feedback mechanism. Regularly evaluate the effectiveness of formulated 
policies and identify existing issues in policy implementation. Based on evaluation results, promptly adjust and improve 
relevant policies to ensure their relevance and effectiveness.

The unique strength of this study lies in its exploration of the impact of technological development policy on the high-quality 
development of the manufacturing industry. While existing research typically treats government technology policy support as a 
controllable variable [62,63]. this paper positions it as a core explanatory variable and examines the role of industrial structure 
thresholds. However, it also has certain limitations, which provide directions for future studies: Future studies could strengthen data 
sources and expand the sample scope, including a more granular analysis of the manufacturing industry by industry categories. 
Additionally, future research could delve deeper into relevant policy recommendations and their implementation to provide more 
comprehensive and effective support for the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry.
